rule: स् becomes ष् after any vowel except अ/आ
explanation: After i, u, ṛ, e, o (and after क् or र्), a following स् retroflexes to ष्. अ and आ do not trigger it, and there are exceptions.

rule: न् becomes ण् after ष् र् or ऋ in the same word
explanation: A preceding ष् र् ऋ retroflexes a later न् to ण्, even across intervening vowels and gutturals/labials. An intervening palatal, cerebral or dental blocks it.

rule: Blocked: an intervening palatal, cerebral or dental stops ṇatva
explanation: The र् of अर्- would retroflex the न् of the ending, but the palatal ज् stands between them and blocks it — hence अर्जुनेन, never अर्जुणेन. Contrast राम + एन → रामेण, where only the labial म् intervenes and does not block.
